title: The Tightest First-Moment Ramsey Bound
description: The classical Erdős (1947) union-bound criterion for diagonal Ramsey numbers, formalized over genuine edge 2-colorings of the complete graph: if 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) then there is a 2-coloring of K_n with no monochromatic K_k, hence R(k,k) > n. This is the tightest bound the first moment method alone can deliver, answering open question #2 of the parent entry.

overview.historicalContext: In a 1947 note in the Bulletin of the AMS, Paul Erdős gave a two-line proof that the diagonal Ramsey number R(k,k) grows at least like 2^(k/2): if the expected number of monochromatic k-cliques in a uniformly random 2-coloring of K_n is below 1, then some coloring has none. This is the founding example of the probabilistic method — proving existence by showing a random object succeeds with positive probability — and it remains, after 75 years, essentially the best known lower bound for diagonal Ramsey numbers (only lower-order improvements by Spencer's alteration and the Lovász Local Lemma are known). The striking feature is that no explicit good coloring is exhibited: the counting argument guarantees one exists. This entry formalizes Erdős's bound in its tightest first-moment form, entirely as finite counting over ℕ with no probability measure.
overview.problemStatement: Answer open question #2 of the parent entry — the tightest Ramsey lower bound achievable by the first moment method alone — over a genuine model of edge colorings. The sample space is all 2-colorings c : Edges n → Bool of the C(n,2) edges of the complete graph on Fin n (there are exactly 2^(C(n,2))). A k-clique K is monochromatic when all C(k,2) of its induced edges share a color. Show: if 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) and 2 ≤ k ≤ n, there exists a 2-coloring of K_n with no monochromatic K_k, hence R(k,k) > n.
overview.proofStrategy: A direct union bound over ℕ, replacing the parent's vacuous placeholder erdos_ramsey_lower_bound. The crux lemma card_mono_le bounds the number of colorings monochromatic on a fixed clique K by 2·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)), via an explicit injection: such a coloring is determined by the common color of the clique's edges together with its values on every edge OUTSIDE the clique (an injection into Bool × (off-clique edges → Bool)). Summing this over the C(n,k) cliques (Finset.card_biUnion_le) bounds the 'bad' colorings by C(n,k)·2·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) = (2·C(n,k))·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)). Splitting 2^(C(n,2)) = 2^(C(k,2))·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) (using C(k,2) ≤ C(n,2)), the hypothesis 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) makes the bad count strictly below the total 2^(C(n,2)), so a non-bad (good) coloring exists, witnessing R(k,k) > n. The concrete instance k=4, n=6 gives 2·C(6,4)=30 < 64=2^(C(4,2)), i.e. R(4,4) > 6, discharged by decide.
keyInsights: The probabilistic method needs no probability here: 'the expected number of monochromatic cliques is < 1' becomes the purely integer statement that the count of bad colorings is below the total 2^(C(n,2)), making Erdős's heuristic fully rigorous and machine-checkable without any measure theory.

The crux is a counting injection, not an inequality on probabilities. A coloring monochromatic on a fixed clique is determined by one bit (the clique's common color) plus its values off the clique — so there are at most 2·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) of them. This 'constant on a sub-family of coordinates ⟹ at most 2·2^(N−|family|)' bound is a reusable first-moment tool.

The threshold 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) is exactly the integer form of the textbook criterion C(n,k)·2^(1−C(k,2)) < 1, and it is the sharpest the pure union bound can give — alteration and the Local Lemma only improve the constant/lower-order terms, which is why R(k,k) ≥ 2^(k/2) has stood essentially unimproved.

Existence without construction: the theorem produces no explicit coloring, only a proof that the good set is nonempty (the bad set cannot exhaust all 2^(C(n,2)) colorings). This is the defining feature of the probabilistic method and is faithfully reflected in the non-constructive ∃ in first_moment_ramsey.

Working over honest edge colorings (functions on the 2-subsets of Fin n) rather than an abstract placeholder is what gives the bound content: the total count 2^(C(n,2)), the clique-edge count C(k,2), and the union bound are all proved, so R(4,4) > 6 comes with a genuine (if non-explicit) witness.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the union-bound (first moment) Ramsey lower bound over real colorings: whenever 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)), the complete graph K_n admits a 2-coloring with no monochromatic K_k, so the diagonal Ramsey number satisfies R(k,k) > n. This is the sharpest bound the first moment method can produce, and it directly answers open question #2 of the parent entry.
conclusion.implications:
**1. Replaces a placeholder with content.** The parent's Ramsey lower bound was a trivial existential; here the bound is proved over an honest model of edge colorings via a genuine counting argument.

**2. The probabilistic method without measure theory.** The entire argument is a finite ℕ counting/union bound — no probability measure is required, making the 'expected number of monochromatic cliques < 1' heuristic fully rigorous and machine-checkable.

**3. Reusable counting infrastructure.** The crux lemma (colorings constant on a sub-family of coordinates number at most 2·2^(N−|family|)) is a general first-moment tool applicable to other existence-by-union-bound arguments.

**4. Concrete witness.** Instantiating at k=4, n=6 gives R(4,4) > 6, with an existence proof of a 2-coloring of K_6 free of monochromatic K_4.
openQuestions: Derive the explicit asymptotic R(k,k) > (1+o(1))·(k/e)·2^(k/2) by estimating C(n,k) and choosing n optimally, showing first moment recovers the classical 2^(k/2) growth.
Formalize the off-diagonal version: 2·C(n,s)·... thresholds giving lower bounds on R(s,t) for s ≠ t via the same union bound.
Quantify the gap to the Lovász Local Lemma bound on the same model, making precise how much the alteration / local-lemma methods improve on the pure first moment.

mainTheorems.name: first_moment_ramsey
mainTheorems.description: If 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) and 2 ≤ k ≤ n, there exists a 2-coloring of the edges of K_n with no monochromatic K_k — i.e. R(k,k) > n.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) (hbound : 2 * n.choose k < 2 ^ (k.choose 2)) : ∃ c : Coloring n, ∀ K : Finset (Fin n), K.card = k → ¬ Mono c K

mainTheorems.name: card_mono_le
mainTheorems.description: Crux count: the number of colorings monochromatic on a fixed clique K with at least one edge is at most 2·2^(C(n,2) − |EdgesIn K|), via an injection into Bool × (off-clique edges → Bool).
mainTheorems.leanType: (hK : (EdgesIn n K).Nonempty) : (univ.filter (Mono · K)).card ≤ 2 * 2 ^ ((Edges n).card - (EdgesIn n K).card)

mainTheorems.name: ramsey_number_gt
mainTheorems.description: Witness form of R(k,k) > n: a coloring in which every k-clique contains two edges of different colors.
mainTheorems.leanType: ∃ c : Coloring n, ∀ K, K.card = k → ∃ e ∈ EdgesIn n K, ∃ f ∈ EdgesIn n K, c e ≠ c f

mainTheorems.name: ramsey_four_gt_six
mainTheorems.description: Concrete instance: 2·C(6,4) = 30 < 64 = 2^(C(4,2)), so K_6 has a 2-coloring with no monochromatic K_4 (R(4,4) > 6).
mainTheorems.leanType: ∃ c : Coloring 6, ∀ K : Finset (Fin 6), K.card = 4 → ¬ Mono c K

sections.title: Edges and Colorings
sections.summary: Edges n is the set of 2-element subsets of Fin n (the edges of K_n), and a Coloring assigns a Bool to each. card_Edges proves there are exactly C(n,2) edges, via Finset.card_powersetCard.

sections.title: Induced Clique Edges
sections.summary: EdgesIn n K is the set of edges contained in a vertex set K. card_EdgesIn proves these biject with the 2-subsets of K (image under coercion equals K.powersetCard 2), so a k-clique has exactly C(k,2) induced edges.

sections.title: Monochromatic Cliques
sections.summary: Mono c K holds when all induced edges of K share one color under c, with a Decidable instance. This is the event whose colorings are counted in the union bound.

sections.title: Crux Count (the Union-Bound Term)
sections.summary: card_mono_le: the colorings monochromatic on a fixed clique K (with at least one edge) number at most 2·2^(C(n,2)−|EdgesIn K|), via an explicit injection ψ into Bool × (off-clique edges → Bool) — a monochromatic coloring is recovered from the clique's common color plus its values off the clique.

sections.title: The First-Moment Ramsey Bound
sections.summary: first_moment_ramsey: union-bounding card_mono_le over the C(n,k) cliques (card_biUnion_le) bounds the bad colorings by (2·C(n,k))·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)); splitting 2^(C(n,2)) and applying 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) shows bad < total, so a good coloring with no monochromatic K_k exists.

sections.title: Ramsey Number Lower Bound and Concrete Witness
sections.summary: ramsey_number_gt restates the bound in witness form (every k-clique has two differently-colored edges), and ramsey_four_gt_six is the concrete decidable instance R(4,4) > 6 (2·C(6,4) = 30 < 64 = 2^(C(4,2))).

crossReferences.description: Parent entry. Answers its open question #2 ('tightest Ramsey bound achievable via the first moment method alone') and replaces its placeholder erdos_ramsey_lower_bound (a vacuous ∃ n ≥ 2^(k/2)) with the genuine union-bound proof over real edge colorings.
The alteration method (delete a vertex from each monochromatic clique) improves on the pure first-moment bound proved here by a lower-order factor.
The Lovász Local Lemma gives a stronger existence criterion on the same edge-coloring model, sharpening the constant in the Ramsey lower bound.

references.label: Erdős 1947

meta.author: Paul Erdős (1947), formalized in Lean 4
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (depends only on the foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no sorryAx, no native_decide / Lean.ofReduceBool).
originalContributions: A genuine model of edge 2-colorings of K_n (functions on the C(n,2) two-element subsets of Fin n), with the total count 2^(C(n,2)) proved.
card_EdgesIn: the induced edges of a vertex set K biject with its 2-subsets, giving exactly C(|K|,2) clique edges.
card_mono_le: the union-bound term — colorings monochromatic on a fixed clique number at most 2·2^(C(n,2)−C(k,2)) — proved by an explicit injection into Bool × (off-clique edges → Bool).
first_moment_ramsey: the tightest first-moment criterion 2·C(n,k) < 2^(C(k,2)) ⟹ ∃ good 2-coloring of K_n ⟹ R(k,k) > n, entirely over ℕ with no probability measure.
ramsey_number_gt: witness reformulation as 'every k-clique has two differently colored edges'.
